purpose: machine-usable expert-system KB of concrete geometric work-units a designer, architect, or planner performs: mensuration, trigonometry, design proportion systems, and coordinate/vector geometry, with scoring, workflow, conflict, risk, verification, and handoff control for session-bounded execution.
assumptions: applied geometry for design/architecture/planning at practitioner grain; not pure mathematical proof
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
structural/load geometry is geometry-only and not a substitute for certified structural engineering
metric/imperial and 2D/3D contexts are both in scope; CRS/datum work covers planning-scale site geometry
exclusions: rigorous proof-based pure geometry and topology
full finite-element or certified structural analysis
advanced differential geometry and tensor calculus
GIS spatial-database operations beyond basic georeferencing

competency_questions.question: Is the spatial task stated as a well-posed objective with units, frame, and tolerance?
Are units and drawing scale converted consistently, including area/volume powers?
How are areas, perimeters, surface areas, and volumes of plane figures and solids computed?
How are right and oblique triangles solved with sine, cosine, and tangent?
How are heights, distances, slopes/grades, and bearings computed in the field?
How are ratio, golden-ratio systems, and modular grids applied to a design composition?
How are points and vectors represented and combined in a coordinate frame?
How are translate/rotate/scale transformations composed correctly?
How is precise, constraint-driven CAD geometry constructed and georeferenced?
How is simple structural/load geometry (force triangles, centroids) resolved without overclaiming?
How is measurement error and tolerance propagated so reported precision is honest?
How are geometric results independently verified before handoff?
In what order should framing, units, computation, verification, and handoff proceed to reduce rework?
When does a proportion or precision claim require labeling or human review rather than assertion?

glossary.definition: the ratio between a drawing dimension and the real dimension it represents
the permissible deviation of a dimension from its nominal value
the branch of geometry concerned with measuring lengths, areas, and volumes
the steepness of a slope expressed as a ratio, percentage, or angle
a direction expressed as an angle from a north reference
the proportion approximately 1.618 used as a compositional construction
a layout structure of repeated modules, columns, gutters, and margins
a quantity with both magnitude and direction, represented by components
a transformation (translate/rotate/scale/shear) preserving lines and parallelism
the geometric center of a figure or the balance point of a uniform body
a coordinate reference system defining how coordinates map to locations
the error by which a measured loop fails to return to its start

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from applied-geometry and engineering-mathematics practice (Elam, Geometry of Design; Stroud & Booth, Engineering Mathematics) and standard design/surveying/CAD convention; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: State the spatial task as a well-posed problem: what is measured/constructed, in what units and coordinate frame, to what tolerance, and for what design/build decision.

excluded: practitioner who computes before fixing units, frame, and tolerance

contradictors: practitioner who computes before fixing units, frame, and tolerance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the design intent, required tolerance, units, or coordinate frame changes

pros.claim: an explicit objective and tolerance prevent over- or under-precise geometry
pros.example: fixing +/-5mm tolerance early stops needless 6-decimal work

pros.claim: naming the decision the geometry serves scopes which quantities matter
pros.example: 'will the stair fit?' selects rise/run/headroom only

cons.claim: framing feels like overhead on a 'simple' calculation
cons.example: a one-off area looks too small to formalize

cons.claim: intent can be ambiguous before measurement begins
cons.example: site dimensions unknown until survey

acceptance_tests: objective stated with units, frame, and a numeric tolerance
each downstream quantity traces to a decision

nodes.definition: Establish and convert units and drawing scale consistently (metric/imperial, scale ratios like 1:50, area/volume unit powers) so every later quantity is dimensionally correct.

excluded: practitioner who mixes mm and m or forgets area scales as the square of length

contradictors: practitioner who mixes mm and m or forgets area scales as the square of length

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when units, scale, or measurement source changes

pros.claim: dimensional analysis catches errors before they propagate
pros.example: mm^2 vs m^2 mismatch caught by unit check

pros.claim: a fixed scale factor makes all scaled drawings mutually consistent
pros.example: 1:50 applied uniformly across a plan set

cons.claim: conversion factors are error-prone when done by hand
cons.example: sqft<->sqm off by 10.76 if length factor reused

cons.claim: scale ambiguity on undimensioned drawings
cons.example: photocopied plan no longer at stated scale

acceptance_tests: all quantities pass a dimensional-consistency check
area uses length^2 and volume length^3 factors

nodes.definition: Compute area and perimeter of plane figures (rectangles, triangles, circles, trapezia, polygons) including composite shapes via decomposition.

excluded: estimator who approximates an irregular plot as a rectangle

contradictors: estimator who approximates an irregular plot as a rectangle

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when shape dimensions or decomposition strategy change

pros.claim: decomposition turns any polygon into summable known shapes
pros.example: an L-room split into two rectangles

pros.claim: closed-form formulas are exact and fast
pros.example: circle area = pi r^2

cons.claim: irregular curved boundaries need approximation
cons.example: a lake outline needs the trapezoidal rule

cons.claim: composite sign errors when subtracting holes
cons.example: forgetting to subtract a courtyard void

acceptance_tests: area recomputed by an independent decomposition matches
perimeter closes (sum of edges = boundary)

nodes.definition: Compute surface area and volume of solids (prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, spheres) and composite solids for material, capacity, and quantity takeoffs.

excluded: estimator who scales volume by a linear factor

contradictors: estimator who scales volume by a linear factor

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when solid geometry, fill assumptions, or units change

pros.claim: volume drives concrete, fill, and capacity quantities directly
pros.example: slab volume = area x thickness for a pour

pros.claim: surface area drives finish, paint, and cladding takeoffs
pros.example: wall area sets paint quantity

cons.claim: composite solids hide internal voids
cons.example: a tank wall thickness ignored in capacity

cons.claim: frusta and partial solids need care
cons.example: a truncated cone volume mis-derived

acceptance_tests: volume recomputed by an independent method matches
capacity cross-checked against a known fill

nodes.definition: Apply angle relationships and triangle properties (angle sums, similarity, congruence, Pythagoras) as the basis for all practical trigonometric work.

excluded: practitioner who assumes a triangle is right-angled without checking

contradictors: practitioner who assumes a triangle is right-angled without checking

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when triangle assumptions (right angle, similarity) change

pros.claim: similarity lets unknown sizes be inferred from known ratios
pros.example: shadow-and-stick height by similar triangles

pros.claim: Pythagoras gives exact distances in right triangles
pros.example: diagonal of a 3-4-5 brace = 5

cons.claim: assuming a right angle that is not present
cons.example: an out-of-square corner breaks Pythagoras

cons.claim: degenerate/ambiguous triangles
cons.example: SSA can yield two triangles

acceptance_tests: angle sum equals 180 deg in each planar triangle
right-angle assumption verified before Pythagoras

nodes.definition: Use sine, cosine, and tangent ratios to solve right triangles for unknown sides and angles.

included: one side + one acute angle or two sides
excluded: practitioner who confuses sin/cos or degree/radian mode

contradictors: practitioner who confuses sin/cos or degree/radian mode
inputs: one side + one acute angle or two sides

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when triangle is non-right or angle-unit mode changes

pros.claim: SOH-CAH-TOA solves any right triangle from minimal data
pros.example: tan(angle)=rise/run for a ramp

pros.claim: inverse ratios recover angles from side lengths
pros.example: atan2 recovers a bearing

cons.claim: degree/radian mode errors are silent
cons.example: calculator in radians gives nonsense angles

cons.claim: only valid for right triangles
cons.example: an oblique triangle needs sine/cosine rule

acceptance_tests: solution satisfies the original ratio definitions
angle unit mode verified

nodes.definition: Solve non-right (oblique) triangles using the law of sines and law of cosines, handling the ambiguous case.

excluded: practitioner who forces right-triangle trig onto an oblique triangle

contradictors: practitioner who forces right-triangle trig onto an oblique triangle

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when data pattern (SSA/SAS/ASA/SSS) or ambiguity changes

pros.claim: law of cosines solves SAS/SSS exactly
pros.example: triangulating a plot from three sides

pros.claim: law of sines extends ratio methods to any triangle
pros.example: find a roof angle from two sides and an angle

cons.claim: SSA ambiguous case yields zero, one, or two triangles
cons.example: two valid roof slopes from one dataset

cons.claim: numerically sensitive near degenerate triangles
cons.example: nearly collinear points lose precision

failure_modes: wrong rule for the data pattern
acceptance_tests: solved triangle satisfies all three angle/side laws
ambiguous case explicitly enumerated

nodes.definition: Apply trigonometry to field problems: heights, distances, angles of elevation/depression, and inaccessible-point measurement.

excluded: practitioner who ignores instrument height or baseline error

contradictors: practitioner who ignores instrument height or baseline error

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when baseline, instrument height, or angle measurements change

pros.claim: angle + baseline reaches otherwise inaccessible heights
pros.example: tower height from a ground angle and distance

pros.claim: two-station methods remove the need to reach the target
pros.example: river width by two-bank angles

cons.claim: forgetting instrument/eye height biases the result
cons.example: tower height under-measured by 1.5 m

cons.claim: small angle errors amplify over long baselines
cons.example: 0.5 deg error over 200 m is meters of height

acceptance_tests: instrument height included in the height result
result cross-checked from a second station

nodes.definition: Express and compute slope/gradient (ratio, percent, degrees) and bearings/azimuths for ramps, drainage, roads, and orientation.

excluded: practitioner who conflates percent grade with degrees

contradictors: practitioner who conflates percent grade with degrees

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reference north, grade convention, or route geometry changes

pros.claim: grade ties geometry to code limits directly
pros.example: an accessible ramp must be <= 1:12 (8.3%)

pros.claim: bearings give a frame-independent orientation
pros.example: azimuth fixes a site axis to true north

cons.claim: percent vs degree vs ratio confusion
cons.example: 10% grade is 5.7 deg, not 10 deg

cons.claim: magnetic vs true vs grid north mismatch
cons.example: bearing off by declination

acceptance_tests: grade reported in all three forms consistently
accessibility/drainage limit checked

nodes.definition: Use ratio and proportion to size, scale, and subdivide design elements consistently across a composition.

excluded: designer who sizes elements by eye without a ratio system

contradictors: designer who sizes elements by eye without a ratio system

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the governing ratio or base dimension changes

pros.claim: a single ratio system unifies many element sizes
pros.example: a 1.5 type-scale sets all heading sizes

pros.claim: proportional scaling preserves relationships under resize
pros.example: a layout scales without redrawing

cons.claim: a chosen ratio may fight functional minimums
cons.example: a proportional door too narrow to use

cons.claim: compounding ratios drift from round buildable sizes
cons.example: fractional millimetre dimensions

acceptance_tests: all element sizes derive from the declared ratio
functional minimums still satisfied

nodes.definition: Apply classical proportion systems (golden ratio, root rectangles, Fibonacci, Modulor) to composition while distinguishing evidence-based use from decorative myth.

excluded: critic who claims the golden ratio is universally optimal or universally meaningless

contradictors: critic who claims the golden ratio is universally optimal or universally meaningless

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a proportion claim is challenged as decorative vs functional

pros.claim: a coherent system gives a defensible compositional logic
pros.example: Elam's golden-section analyses of posters

pros.claim: root rectangles tile and subdivide cleanly
pros.example: root-2 keeps aspect ratio under halving

cons.claim: overclaimed as a law of beauty without evidence
cons.example: retrofitting phi onto any pleasing layout

cons.claim: forcing phi can override function and grid
cons.example: a phi column too slender to carry load

acceptance_tests: each proportion claim labelled compositional not empirical
system does not violate functional limits

nodes.definition: Construct modular grids, columns, gutters, baseline grids, and the rule of thirds to organize layout space.

excluded: designer who places elements with no underlying grid

contradictors: designer who places elements with no underlying grid

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when canvas size, column count, or margin policy changes

pros.claim: a grid makes alignment and rhythm systematic
pros.example: a 12-column grid aligns a whole page set

pros.claim: the rule of thirds places focal points predictably
pros.example: subject on a thirds intersection

cons.claim: a rigid grid can suppress needed emphasis
cons.example: hero element broken out of grid intentionally

cons.claim: module math fails when content does not fit
cons.example: an odd image breaks a 12-col fit

failure_modes: grid math does not close to the canvas
acceptance_tests: columns + gutters + margins sum to canvas width
baseline grid divides the text block evenly

nodes.definition: Place points, distances, midpoints, lines, and slopes in a Cartesian frame as the substrate for CAD and analytic geometry.

excluded: practitioner who works without a defined origin or axis convention

contradictors: practitioner who works without a defined origin or axis convention

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when origin, axis orientation, or handedness changes

pros.claim: coordinates make geometry computable and exact
pros.example: distance formula gives an exact span

pros.claim: a shared frame lets disciplines overlay drawings
pros.example: arch and structural models align on one origin

cons.claim: axis/handedness conventions differ across tools
cons.example: y-down in screens vs y-up in CAD

cons.claim: origin choice affects every downstream number
cons.example: a shifted origin offsets all coordinates

acceptance_tests: origin, axis directions, and handedness recorded
a known distance reproduces via the formula

nodes.definition: Represent and combine vectors (addition, scaling, dot/cross products, magnitude, direction) for displacement, force-direction, and orientation problems.

excluded: practitioner who adds vectors component-wise across mismatched frames

contradictors: practitioner who adds vectors component-wise across mismatched frames

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the working frame or vector convention changes

pros.claim: vectors unify direction and magnitude in one object
pros.example: a displacement and a force share the math

pros.claim: dot/cross products give angles, areas, and normals
pros.example: cross product yields a surface normal

cons.claim: frame mismatches corrupt component arithmetic
cons.example: adding world and local vectors directly

cons.claim: 2D cross product is a scalar, easy to mishandle
cons.example: sign of the 2D cross misread

failure_modes: unnormalized direction used as unit vector
acceptance_tests: operands share a frame before combination
unit vectors verified to have magnitude 1

nodes.definition: Apply geometric transformations (translate, rotate, scale, reflect, shear) and their composition order to position and modify geometry.

excluded: practitioner who assumes transformation order does not matter

contradictors: practitioner who assumes transformation order does not matter

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when transform order, pivot, or non-uniform scaling changes

pros.claim: composed transforms reposition geometry exactly
pros.example: rotate-about-a-point = translate, rotate, translate back

pros.claim: matrices make repeated transforms efficient
pros.example: one matrix applies a full transform chain

cons.claim: order matters: rotate-then-translate != translate-then-rotate
cons.example: wrong order misplaces a part

cons.claim: non-uniform scale distorts angles and normals
cons.example: a circle scaled to an ellipse breaks a fit

failure_modes: non-uniform scale applied to rotated geometry
acceptance_tests: composition order documented and reproducible
a round-trip inverse returns the original geometry

nodes.definition: Construct precise CAD geometry with constraints, snaps, layers, and reference geometry so drawings are dimensionally driven, not eyeballed.

excluded: drafter who places lines by visual snapping without constraints

contradictors: drafter who places lines by visual snapping without constraints

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when drafting standard, constraint scheme, or base frame changes

pros.claim: constraint-driven geometry updates consistently on edit
pros.example: change one dimension, the model adapts

pros.claim: snaps and layers keep complex drawings coherent
pros.example: reference layers prevent stray geometry

cons.claim: over-constraint locks the model and blocks edits
cons.example: conflicting constraints freeze a sketch

cons.claim: visual snapping without constraints drifts off-grid
cons.example: a wall 0.3 mm off true alignment

acceptance_tests: key dimensions are constraint-driven
model regenerates correctly after a parameter change

nodes.definition: Resolve simple structural geometry: force triangles, resultants, centroid/center-of-mass, and load paths via vector and triangle methods (geometry only, not full structural design).

excluded: practitioner who treats simplified load geometry as a full structural check

contradictors: practitioner who treats simplified load geometry as a full structural check

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when load magnitude/direction, geometry, or safety scope changes

pros.claim: force triangles resolve simple equilibrium fast
pros.example: a two-cable load split by a triangle of forces

pros.claim: centroid locates balance and load distribution
pros.example: centroid of a section for a stability check

cons.claim: geometry alone is not a safety-rated structural design
cons.example: mistaking a sketch for an engineered check

cons.claim: 3D load paths exceed simple triangle methods
cons.example: a spatial truss needs full analysis

failure_modes: simplified geometry treated as certified design
acceptance_tests: force polygon closes for equilibrium
result flagged as geometry-only, not certified design

nodes.definition: Track measurement error, rounding, and tolerance through geometric computations so reported precision is honest and fit-for-purpose.

excluded: practitioner who reports six decimals from a tape measure

contradictors: practitioner who reports six decimals from a tape measure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when input precision, tolerance, or computation chain changes

pros.claim: error tracking prevents false precision and bad fits
pros.example: reporting 12.3 m not 12.34567 m

pros.claim: tolerance stack-up reveals whether parts will assemble
pros.example: summed clearances exceed the gap

cons.claim: rigorous propagation is effortful for quick jobs
cons.example: a back-of-envelope estimate skips it

cons.claim: worst-case stacking can be overly conservative
cons.example: over-tight tolerance raises cost

acceptance_tests: reported figures match input precision
tolerance stack-up checked against the spec

nodes.definition: Verify geometric results with independent checks: closure, redundant measurement, dimensional consistency, unit sanity, and reasonableness bounds.

excluded: practitioner who trusts a single computation without a check

contradictors: practitioner who trusts a single computation without a check

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a result is challenged or a check fails closure

pros.claim: independent checks catch the errors a single method hides
pros.example: a second method exposes a unit slip

pros.claim: closure quantifies survey/loop quality
pros.example: a traverse closing to 1:5000 is acceptable

cons.claim: verification adds time before sign-off
cons.example: a deadline tempts skipping the check

cons.claim: a check sharing the same error is not independent
cons.example: reusing the same wrong constant

acceptance_tests: each critical result has an independent recomputation
closure within the stated tolerance

nodes.definition: Package verified geometry into a reusable handoff: dimensioned drawing/coordinate set, assumptions, tolerances, units, and provenance for downstream design or fabrication.

excluded: practitioner who hands off numbers without units, frame, or tolerance

contradictors: practitioner who hands off numbers without units, frame, or tolerance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when downstream consumers, tolerance, or units change

pros.claim: a complete handoff prevents downstream re-measurement
pros.example: fabricator builds from the package alone

pros.claim: recorded assumptions make later changes traceable
pros.example: a tolerance note explains a later refit

cons.claim: packaging is overhead when reuse seems unlikely
cons.example: a one-off sketch skips documentation

cons.claim: a stale handoff misleads if upstream changes
cons.example: an old coordinate set used after a redesign

acceptance_tests: package carries units, frame, tolerance, and assumptions
provenance and verification status recorded

nodes.definition: Choose and reconcile coordinate systems and georeferencing (local site grid, projected CRS, datum) for planning and site geometry without distortion error.

excluded: practitioner who mixes a local grid with a projected CRS unknowingly

contradictors: practitioner who mixes a local grid with a projected CRS unknowingly

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when CRS, datum, or control-point set changes

pros.claim: a declared CRS lets site geometry align with maps and other datasets
pros.example: plan overlays the cadastral base correctly

pros.claim: control points tie a local grid to the wider world
pros.example: site grid georeferenced to national datum

cons.claim: projection distortion biases distances and areas over large extents
cons.example: a long boundary mis-measured on the wrong CRS

cons.claim: datum mismatches shift positions by meters
cons.example: WGS84 vs a local datum offset

acceptance_tests: CRS and datum explicitly recorded
control points reproduce within tolerance

edges.why_related: the objective and tolerance define which units and scale are needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing units before framing fixes the wrong precision
edges.example: a +/-5mm tolerance picks mm units

edges.why_related: the spatial objective and frame spec define the coordinate substrate
edges.risk_of_conflict: placing a frame before framing the task mislocates origin
edges.example: origin chosen to suit the build datum
edges.resolution_rule: frame the task before fixing the origin

edges.why_related: the stated tolerance defines the precision budget tracked downstream
edges.benefit_of_coupling: error tracking matched to the spec
edges.risk_of_conflict: tracking error without a tolerance target is unanchored
edges.example: tolerance spec seeds the sig-fig policy

edges.why_related: consistent units are required before any area/perimeter value is valid
edges.risk_of_conflict: area computed in mixed units is wrong
edges.example: mm and m mixed yields a 1000x error

edges.why_related: a consistent unit/scale base is needed before proportioning dimensions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ratios applied to a stable base
edges.risk_of_conflict: proportioning across scales mixes magnitudes
edges.example: a 1:50 element sized against full-scale

edges.why_related: planar areas are building blocks for surface area and volume of solids
edges.risk_of_conflict: volume from a wrong face area is wrong
edges.example: prism volume = base area x height
edges.resolution_rule: get face areas right before volume

edges.why_related: the framed problem fixes which angles/triangles are in scope
edges.benefit_of_coupling: triangle work scoped to the task
edges.risk_of_conflict: solving arbitrary triangles wastes effort
edges.example: only the roof triangle matters here

edges.why_related: triangle classification and Pythagoras underpin sine/cosine/tangent ratios
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ratios applied to verified right triangles
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying ratios to a non-right triangle is invalid
edges.example: confirm the right angle before tan=rise/run

edges.why_related: right-triangle ratios generalize into the sine and cosine rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: forcing right-triangle trig onto oblique data fails
edges.example: an oblique roof needs the cosine rule

edges.why_related: elevation/depression problems are right-triangle trig applied in the field
edges.risk_of_conflict: field error if the underlying trig is shaky
edges.example: tower height from a ground angle
edges.resolution_rule: secure the trig before field use

edges.why_related: two-station and non-right field problems need the sine/cosine rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: two-station methods fail without oblique laws
edges.example: river width by two-bank angles
edges.resolution_rule: have oblique laws ready for field use

edges.why_related: grade and bearing are right-triangle ratios of rise, run, and direction
edges.risk_of_conflict: grade errors if rise/run trig is wrong
edges.example: tan(angle)=rise/run for a ramp

edges.why_related: proportion systems are specific ratio constructions
edges.risk_of_conflict: misapplied phi if ratio basics are weak
edges.example: root-2 rectangle from a unit square

edges.why_related: grids are ratio systems applied to layout space
edges.risk_of_conflict: grid math fails without ratio discipline
edges.example: columns sized by a consistent ratio

edges.why_related: vectors are defined by components in a coordinate frame
edges.benefit_of_coupling: vector ops in a stable frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: frame-less vectors corrupt arithmetic
edges.example: displacement as a coordinate difference

edges.why_related: transformations act on coordinates relative to an origin/axes
edges.risk_of_conflict: transforms without a frame misplace geometry
edges.example: rotate about a defined origin

edges.why_related: translation, rotation, and scaling are vector/matrix operations
edges.risk_of_conflict: transform errors from shaky vector ops
edges.example: translate by a displacement vector

edges.why_related: CAD geometry is constructed on a coordinate frame
edges.benefit_of_coupling: constraint-driven CAD on a real frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: eyeballed CAD drifts off the frame
edges.example: constraints anchored to the origin
edges.resolution_rule: fix the frame before CAD construction

edges.why_related: CAD assembly relies on correct transform composition
edges.risk_of_conflict: misordered transforms misplace CAD parts
edges.example: array via repeated transforms
edges.resolution_rule: get transform order right in CAD

edges.why_related: force resolution is vector addition and projection
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong forces from shaky vector ops
edges.example: resultant of two cable forces

edges.why_related: force triangles use triangle geometry for equilibrium
edges.risk_of_conflict: open force triangle means unbalanced loads
edges.example: triangle of forces for a tie
edges.resolution_rule: ground load geometry in triangle basics

edges.why_related: georeferencing maps a local Cartesian frame onto a projected CRS
edges.benefit_of_coupling: site grid tied to the world
edges.risk_of_conflict: CRS confusion from an undefined local frame
edges.example: local grid georeferenced to a datum
edges.resolution_rule: define the local frame before georeferencing

edges.why_related: verification thresholds come from the propagated error budget
edges.risk_of_conflict: verification without a budget is arbitrary
edges.example: closure judged against expected error
edges.resolution_rule: set the error budget before verifying

edges.why_related: areas are independently re-derived during verification
edges.risk_of_conflict: unverified areas carry silent errors
edges.example: area recomputed by a second split

edges.why_related: field heights/distances are checked from a second station
edges.risk_of_conflict: single-station field errors persist
edges.example: height re-measured from another base

edges.why_related: only verified geometry may be packaged for handoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: handing off unverified geometry causes rework
edges.example: verified coords released to a fabricator

edges.why_related: the CAD model is the carrier of the handoff geometry
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unconstrained model misleads downstream
edges.example: drawing set issued for build

edges.why_related: the handoff must declare the units and scale used
edges.risk_of_conflict: unit-less handoff causes scale errors
edges.example: scale and units stated on the sheet

edges.why_related: rounding during unit conversion changes the propagated error
edges.risk_of_conflict: mid-chain rounding inflates error
edges.example: rounding before conversion loses digits
edges.resolution_rule: convert at full precision, round at the end

edges.why_related: member slope sets the direction of resolved forces
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong slope misdirects forces
edges.example: a braced angle sets force components
edges.resolution_rule: use the true member slope in resolution

edges.why_related: projection distortion bounds the accuracy of computed site areas
edges.risk_of_conflict: distorted areas over large extents
edges.example: a long boundary area biased by projection
edges.resolution_rule: compute large-extent areas in an equal-area CRS

edges.why_related: a failed verification can trigger revisiting the transform chain
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-transform loops
edges.example: a non-closing round-trip flags a bad order; stop after the inverse matches
edges.resolution_rule: revisit transforms on failure; stop when the inverse round-trip matches

edges.why_related: verification failure can reopen the framing (tolerance or scope)
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless reframing
edges.example: persistent closure failure reopens the tolerance spec; stop when one frame passes verification
edges.resolution_rule: reopen framing only on repeated failure; stop after a passing frame

edges.why_related: both decompose direction into components via sine/cosine
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating the two methods
edges.example: vector components are r*cos and r*sin
edges.resolution_rule: use whichever representation the task favors; keep them distinct

edges.why_related: a decorative proportion system can fight a functional ratio requirement
edges.risk_of_conflict: function sacrificed for an aesthetic ratio
edges.example: a phi column too slender to carry load

edges.why_related: an accessibility/drainage grade limit can conflict with a desired proportional form
edges.risk_of_conflict: a too-steep ramp to keep a proportion
edges.example: a 1:8 ramp wanted but 1:12 required
edges.resolution_rule: code grade limits dominate proportional preference

edges.why_related: CAD's apparent infinite precision tempts reporting beyond real tolerance
edges.risk_of_conflict: 6-decimal CAD output from tape measurements
edges.example: model shows 12.34567 m from a +/-10mm tape
edges.resolution_rule: report only to the justified tolerance

edges.why_related: non-uniform scaling distorts angles, invalidating force directions
edges.risk_of_conflict: a non-uniformly scaled brace misreports forces
edges.example: an ellipse-scaled member skews load angles
edges.resolution_rule: forbid non-uniform scale where force angles matter

edges.why_related: schedule pressure to hand off conflicts with completing verification
edges.risk_of_conflict: handing off before closure checks
edges.example: deadline tempts skipping a second check

edges.why_related: simplified load geometry may be mistaken for a certified structural result in the handoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: a sketch passed off as engineered design
edges.example: load-path sketch reused as a safety check
edges.resolution_rule: handoff must flag geometry-only, not certified design

conflict_axes.trigger: a proportion system forces a dimension below a functional or structural minimum
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: functional and structural minimums dominate; proportion is optimized subject to them
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a layout is required to be both phi-exact and below a structural minimum
conflict_axes.example: a golden-section column is too slender to carry the load

conflict_axes.trigger: CAD precision exceeds the precision justified by measurement tolerance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: real measurement tolerance dominates apparent CAD precision
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: outputs reported to more digits than any input supports
conflict_axes.example: a model shows 12.34567 m from a +/-10mm tape

conflict_axes.trigger: a deadline pressures handing off geometry before independent checks complete
resolution_order: escalate if the deadline cannot accommodate verification
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: verification dominates speed; no handoff before checks pass
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a deadline forces release of unverified geometry
conflict_axes.example: coordinates released without a second-method check

conflict_axes.trigger: a desired form needs a grade steeper than an accessibility or drainage limit
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: code grade limits dominate desired form
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a ramp must be both 1:8 for form and 1:12 for access
conflict_axes.example: an accessible ramp capped at 1:12 overrides a steeper aesthetic

conflict_axes.trigger: non-uniform scaling is applied where angles and force directions must be preserved
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: angle and force preservation dominates convenience of non-uniform scaling
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a load-bearing member is non-uniformly scaled
conflict_axes.example: a brace scaled to an ellipse skews its load angle

conflict_axes.trigger: a local grid is mixed with a projected CRS over a large extent
resolution_order: use an equal-area CRS for large-extent areas
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: declared CRS consistency dominates ad-hoc local convenience for large extents
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: site geometry spans an extent where projection distortion is material
conflict_axes.example: a long boundary length differs between local grid and projected CRS

conflict_axes.trigger: simplified load geometry is treated as a certified structural result
resolution_order: route safety claims to qualified engineering
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety scope dominates; geometry-only results must not be presented as certified design
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a load-path sketch is used as a safety justification
conflict_axes.example: a force-triangle sketch reused as a structural sign-off

conflict_axes.trigger: added geometric detail exceeds what the tolerance budget can justify
resolution_order: model detail only to that budget
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: tolerance budget dominates ornamental modeling detail
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: detail is modeled finer than the measurement tolerance
conflict_axes.example: sub-millimetre fillets modeled from a tape-measured survey

conflict_axes.trigger: a late change to origin, axes, or units forces rework of dependent geometry
resolution_order: run impact analysis before changing it
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: early frame stability dominates; changes require impact analysis and revalidation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: origin/axis change requested after downstream geometry is built
conflict_axes.example: shifting the origin after the CAD model is constructed

edge_cases.trigger: lengths in mm and m combined in one computation
edge_cases.example: a wall length in mm multiplied by a height in m
edge_cases.detection_method: run a dimensional-consistency check on every product/quotient
resolution: normalize all inputs to one unit first
add a unit assertion before arithmetic

edge_cases.trigger: area or volume converted with a linear scale factor
edge_cases.failure_mode: area off by factor^2, volume by factor^3
edge_cases.example: sqft->sqm using the length factor 3.28 not 10.76
edge_cases.detection_method: compare against the correct power-of-factor conversion
resolution: apply factor^2 for area and factor^3 for volume
unit-test conversions against known equivalents

edge_cases.trigger: sine/cosine/tangent applied to a non-right triangle
edge_cases.example: assuming a right angle at an out-of-square corner
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the right angle before using SOH-CAH-TOA
resolution: confirm the right angle or switch to oblique laws
flag unverified right-angle assumptions

edge_cases.trigger: SSA data admits two valid triangles
edge_cases.example: two roof slopes satisfy the same side-side-angle data
edge_cases.detection_method: enumerate both solutions of the ambiguous case
resolution: list zero/one/two solutions explicitly
carry both unless one is physically excluded

edge_cases.trigger: calculator/tool in the wrong angle-unit mode
edge_cases.failure_mode: angles off by the deg/rad factor
edge_cases.example: computing a slope in radian mode when degrees were intended
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check one angle against a known reference value
resolution: set and verify the angle-unit mode
annotate the unit on every angle

edge_cases.trigger: instrument/eye height omitted from a height computation
edge_cases.failure_mode: height under- or over-stated by the instrument height
edge_cases.example: a tower height short by the 1.5 m instrument height
edge_cases.detection_method: add a known-baseline check including instrument height
resolution: add instrument height to the trig result
verify from a second station

edge_cases.trigger: transformations composed in the wrong order
edge_cases.failure_mode: geometry rotated/translated to the wrong place
edge_cases.detection_method: verify a round-trip inverse returns the original geometry
resolution: document and fix composition order
test inverse round-trip equals identity

edge_cases.trigger: non-uniform scale applied to angle/force-critical geometry
edge_cases.example: a member scaled into an ellipse misreports its load angle
edge_cases.detection_method: check angle preservation after any scaling
resolution: forbid non-uniform scale on critical geometry
remodel with uniform scale

edge_cases.trigger: results reported to more digits than tolerance supports
edge_cases.example: a CAD readout of 12.34567 m from a tape measurement
edge_cases.detection_method: compare reported sig-figs to input precision
resolution: round outputs to the justified tolerance
state the precision basis

edge_cases.trigger: a local grid mixed with a projected CRS or wrong datum
edge_cases.example: WGS84 coordinates overlaid on a local-datum site grid
edge_cases.detection_method: reproject control points and check residuals
resolution: declare CRS/datum and transform consistently
verify against control points

edge_cases.trigger: the verification check reuses the same erroneous method/constant
edge_cases.example: re-deriving an area with the same wrong formula
resolution: use a different method or operator for the check
cross-check against a closed-form bound

edge_cases.trigger: a handoff package is reused after upstream geometry changed
edge_cases.example: an old coordinate set used after a redesign
edge_cases.detection_method: check the handoff version/timestamp against the source
resolution: invalidate stale packages on upstream change
stamp provenance and version on every handoff

workflow.objective: fix the spatial objective, units, scale, frame, and tolerance
acceptance_tests: objective stated with units, frame, and tolerance
quantities trace to a decision
workflow.do_first_because: the objective, units, and frame are the highest-coupling foundation all later work inherits

workflow.objective: establish the coordinate frame and, if needed, CRS/datum
acceptance_tests: origin, axes, handedness recorded
control points reproduce within tolerance
workflow.do_first_because: every coordinate, vector, and transform inherits the frame, so it must stabilize before downstream geometry

workflow.objective: compute areas, perimeters, surface areas, and volumes
acceptance_tests: independent recomputation matches
voids subtracted
workflow.do_first_because: mensuration outputs feed quantity, capacity, and material decisions early

workflow.objective: resolve angles, triangles, heights, distances, grades, and bearings
acceptance_tests: angle sums equal 180 deg
results cross-checked from a second station
workflow.do_first_because: trigonometric results gate field feasibility (heights, slopes, access) before committing form

workflow.objective: apply ratio, proportion systems, and modular grids to the composition
acceptance_tests: element sizes derive from the declared ratio
functional minimums satisfied
workflow.do_first_because: proportion choices shape later CAD geometry, so resolve them before constraint modeling

workflow.objective: set up vectors and transformation chains in the frame
acceptance_tests: operands share a frame
inverse round-trip returns the original
workflow.do_first_because: transforms must be correct before CAD assembly and load geometry depend on them

acceptance_tests: key dimensions are constraint-driven
model regenerates after a parameter change
workflow.do_first_because: the CAD model carries the geometry into verification and handoff

workflow.objective: resolve simple force triangles, resultants, and centroids (geometry-only)
acceptance_tests: force polygon closes
result flagged geometry-only not certified design
workflow.do_first_because: load geometry is high-risk and must be explicitly scoped before any handoff

workflow.objective: propagate error, then verify all critical results independently
acceptance_tests: each critical result independently recomputed
closure within tolerance
workflow.do_first_because: nothing may be locked or handed off before independent verification passes

workflow.objective: package verified geometry with units, frame, tolerance, assumptions, and provenance
acceptance_tests: package carries units, frame, tolerance, assumptions
provenance and verification status recorded
workflow.do_first_because: a complete, verified handoff prevents downstream re-measurement and rework

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk geometric result is pressured to ship faster
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk results (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) must pass acceptance tests and human review before release
dominance_rules.required_action: gate the result behind tests and review
dominance_rules.example: a load-geometry sketch held until verified and labelled

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is requested before its prerequisites
dominance_rules.example: compute coordinates before transforms even if transforms feel higher-value

dominance_rules.trigger: a result is about to be locked or handed off without independent checks
dominance_rules.rule: verification must pass before any soft/hard lock or handoff
dominance_rules.required_action: run an independent check before locking

dominance_rules.rule: reported precision is bounded by real measurement tolerance
dominance_rules.required_action: round outputs to the justified tolerance
dominance_rules.example: report 12.3 m not 12.34567 m from a tape

dominance_rules.trigger: an aesthetic proportion violates a functional/structural minimum
dominance_rules.rule: functional and structural minimums dominate proportion systems
dominance_rules.required_action: resize within the minimum and label the concession
dominance_rules.example: widen a phi column to carry its load

dominance_rules.trigger: a desired form needs a non-compliant grade
dominance_rules.rule: code accessibility/drainage grade limits dominate desired form
dominance_rules.required_action: apply the grade limit and reshape the form

dominance_rules.trigger: simplified load geometry is used as a certified result
dominance_rules.rule: geometry-only results must not be presented as certified structural design
dominance_rules.required_action: label geometry-only and route safety claims to engineering
dominance_rules.example: flag a force-triangle sketch as non-certified

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric value implies more certainty than its source supports
dominance_rules.rule: evidence labelling dominates numeric precision; heuristic values stay labelled heuristic
dominance_rules.required_action: keep heuristic labels and avoid false certainty
dominance_rules.example: do not relabel a heuristic estimate as observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a late origin/axis/unit change is requested
dominance_rules.rule: a soft-locked frame changes only after impact analysis and revalidation
dominance_rules.required_action: run impact analysis before changing the frame
dominance_rules.example: re-derive dependents if the origin shifts

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting tempts prose or markdown in a machine artifact
dominance_rules.rule: strict JSON validity dominates prose styling in deliverables
dominance_rules.example: no markdown in the KB file

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or safety-critical geometric decision is automated
dominance_rules.rule: human review overrides automation for irreversible or safety-critical geometry
dominance_rules.example: human sign-off before a fabrication handoff is hard-locked

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix units, frame, and tolerance before any computation
anti_rework_rules.rationale: computing before the frame is set fixes the wrong precision and units
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: arithmetic started before the unit/frame spec exists
anti_rework_rules.example: areas computed before units were normalized

anti_rework_rules.rule: normalize units before computing areas and volumes
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a product mixes mm and m
anti_rework_rules.example: a volume mixing cm and m inputs

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify the triangle (right vs oblique) before choosing trig methods
anti_rework_rules.rationale: applying right-triangle ratios to an oblique triangle yields silent errors
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: ratios used without a verified right angle

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the coordinate frame before vectors and transforms
anti_rework_rules.rationale: frame-less vectors and transforms misplace geometry
anti_rework_rules.example: world and local vectors summed directly

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm functional minimums before applying proportion systems
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a proportion forced below a minimum must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an element sized purely by ratio is unusable
anti_rework_rules.example: a phi column too slender to carry load

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix transform composition order before applying transforms in CAD
anti_rework_rules.rationale: wrong order misplaces geometry and forces rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: parts appear in the wrong location after transforms

anti_rework_rules.rule: label simplified load geometry as geometry-only before any handoff
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unlabeled sketch can be mistaken for certified design
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a load sketch lacks a scope disclaimer
anti_rework_rules.example: a force triangle reused as a safety check

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish the error/tolerance budget before verifying results
anti_rework_rules.rationale: verification without a budget is arbitrary
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: checks run with no pass/fail threshold
anti_rework_rules.example: closure judged with no expected-error bound

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify all critical results before packaging the handoff
anti_rework_rules.rationale: handing off unverified geometry causes downstream rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a package is built before independent checks pass
anti_rework_rules.example: coordinates released without a second-method check

anti_rework_rules.rule: record provenance, units, and assumptions before hard-locking the handoff
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an undocumented handoff cannot be safely reused or changed
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a package omits units, frame, or tolerance
anti_rework_rules.example: a coordinate set issued without its CRS

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validator or design review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.trigger: multiple defects are open at once
iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk_score and downstream coupling
action: score defects by risk and coupling
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defect addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold low-risk defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a soft-locked or high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents via edges and node.dependencies
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the change identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across two passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a classified defect needs an owner
acceptance_tests: each defect routed and repaired

iteration_protocol.trigger: metrics or inputs to a formula changed
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the formula script over nodes and edges
acceptance_tests: validator formula.consistency passes within 0.02
no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a revised prior appears
acceptance_tests: posterior consistent with the no-observed-data formula
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an unresolved high-risk or irreversibility defect persists
acceptance_tests: a recorded human decision exists
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human review recorded or defect resolved

hard lock of the spatial-output handoff

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked handoff or claim change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream frame/unit/assumption changes
